limits.management: Reuses SessionTitleEditor, SessionRenameDialog and SessionDropdownMenu. Inline and dialog renames use local simulated responses only; failures keep dialog input. Branching stays disabled. Archive/delete expose the existing menu and its callback only, without confirmation/execution hosts. No real conversation or file is changed. Actions are disabled without a session identity. Switching state/language resets samples. Full archive/delete lifecycles and rules remain pending confirmation.
limits.research: Reuses ResearchContext for current/candidate directions, expansion/collapse and empty-content hiding. Keeps existing protocol-heading parsing and the first research-channel entry. Collapsed text shows at most three directions; expansion shows original text. No direction selection, generation or persistence is added. Protocol marker display, formatting and presentation beyond three directions remain pending confirmation.
limits.queue: Extracts the existing Composer queue presentation into ComposerQueue in the same business file, reused by the real Composer. APIs, sending and persistence remain in the original flow. Samples enable only expansion, local editing and removal. Steer, resend, reconcile and unknown-result confirmation stay disabled without callbacks; existing state and permission gates still apply. The edit area reuses the editor but saves text in page memory only, not reference changes or server receipts. Resource waits, submission, failure, unknown-result blocking and empty queues are fixed snapshots; real submissions, races and lifecycles are not verified here.
limits.editor: Reuses ComposerEditor, an independent draft store and the existing Composer height limit. Supports local typing, newlines, scrolling, reset, accepting/dismissing a static sample prediction, read-only and disabled states. This is the editor only, not the full Composer: no model prediction, sending, queueing or uploading. The full send toolbar, stop, permissions and queued messages remain coupled to business logic and are not extracted. Complete real-host IME acceptance remains a gap. Switching state or language resets the draft.
limits.taskstatus: Reuses TaskStatus inline and badge variants for running, waiting, failure and unread completion, including existing hidden states for viewed completion and abandonment. State buttons only select sample snapshots, never update real tasks or unread records. Hover hints follow the current implementation; keyboard reachability of the icon remains a gap. No recovery, retry or notification capability is fabricated.
limits.background: Reuses StatusStrip expansion and collapse for active, succeeded, failed, timed-out, cancelled and lost sample tasks. No memory/constraint channels are seeded, and no real task is started, stopped or retried. States are independent snapshots, not executed lifecycles. The existing strip labels all terminal tasks as completed, which does not mean all succeeded. Counting semantics, terminal summary wording, keyboard and focus feedback remain pending confirmation and are not changed here.
limits.suggestions: Reuses NextSteps and the current StoreProvider submission registry. Options or free text record a local simulated submission only; pending disables actions, acceptance consumes the sample once, rejection keeps input, and old cards are inactive. No real Composer, sending or new turn. Real draft preservation, generated suggestions and session re-entry are not verified here. Switching state or language rebuilds the sample.
limits.citations: Reuses CitationLink and CitationSources for inline citations, source lists, structured excerpts, changed/unavailable sources and load failures. Resolution returns local mock data with can_open_pdf=false; it never claims precise navigation or opens real PDFs. Web links, precise navigation, region images, real revision checks and recovery remain gaps. Rechecking only repeats local resolution, not successful navigation. Existing hover previews may coexist with the citation-state dialog; overlay exclusivity remains a gap.
limits.artifacts: Reuses ArtifactEntry cards, version menus and action menus. Existing Dialog and Markdown show static samples. No session/project write target or real path is supplied, so import, save as, copy path, system open and reveal stay disabled. Version selection changes only a sample ID, not historical file content. Real file previews, artifact grouping, export and import lifecycles remain gaps.
limits.messages: Reuses the real conversation Stream: preserves user text and line breaks, recognizes HTTP/HTTPS links, and fades long messages with expand/collapse controls. Hovering or focusing a message reveals copy actions and the user message timestamp; latest answer actions stay visible, while historical answer actions appear on hover or focus. Copy uses the real clipboard with success or failure feedback; links open an external browser. Content and timestamps are samples; no model requests are sent.
limits.attachments: Reuses ComposerAttachments and ComposerSkillRefs with removable and resettable samples. Existing file labels do not imply thumbnail groups, a grouped image viewer or complete file menus.
limits.tools: Reuses the real Stream, Composer and three-level disclosure for execution, answer streaming, completion, failures, user pauses and web search. Use the original controls to open the process and group, show more results, collapse them or fold details. Content, queries and timing are isolated samples; no model, command or real retry runs.
limits.plan: Reuses TodoPanel for running, completed and failed plans with expandable steps. No real resume action; time appears only when supported by existing timing evidence.
limits.receipts: Reuses Stream interaction_reply for answered and skipped receipts. State buttons only select samples, never submit answers or approvals.
limits.approval: Reuses full-text and literature-review authorization policies, confirmation cards and receipts. Seven states cover pending, authorized and rejected with or without checkboxes, plus an expired card. Isolated simulation only: no full-text reads, imports or task continuation.
limits.clarification: PRD pending, submitted and skipped states reuse the product clarification card: recommended drafts, supplementary text, continuous scrolling, question navigation and always-visible receipts. State controls select simulated samples, not real model acceptance.
limits.context: Reuses ContextOption, ComposerRefChip, AssistantContextQuote, SessionReference and Stream. Add, deduplicate and remove affect only this draft; previewing never adds or sends. Sent and unavailable states are independent simulated snapshots; switching state resets the draft. Article-level selection grouping, annotation groups, select-all, image groups, full layered layout and real document/conversation navigation remain gaps. Sent source-opening actions stay disabled; location only exposes the existing callback and anchor.

toast.title: General notification
toast.longDescription: This notification demonstrates an unusually long description using a fictional research workflow. It does not represent a real operation. A researcher might import many documents, inspect their metadata, compare different versions, and organize relevant resources into a project. Some records may be missing authors or publication dates, while others may contain duplicate titles or incomplete identifiers. Detailed feedback about these conditions can require considerably more space than a short confirmation. This example includes background information, processing notes, and suggested next steps so that the notification can be observed with realistic overflow. Check whether the description truncates cleanly at the existing line limit without pushing the title, icon, or close button out of position. When the window becomes narrower, the notification should respect its normal width constraints instead of expanding across the page. Light and dark themes should preserve readable text and a clear distinction between the title and supporting content. Multiple notifications should remain independent, and dismissing one should not change the others. This is static demonstration text only: it does not upload documents, update metadata, create projects, or send task messages. Use this example alongside the default and title-only notifications to compare how the component presents different amounts of information.
